newsitem.title: INDIA: India says oil price decision soon, options open.
newsitem.headline: India says oil price decision soon, options open.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday said it would soon take a decision on the hike in prices of petroleum products after consultations with the United Front steering committee, local news agencies reported.

Both United News of India and Press Trust of India quoted a government spokesman as clarifying a statement by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral in which he had said that subsidies on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and diesel would be slashed.

UNI quoted government spokesman as saying: "The Prime Minister in a television interview had said that increase in the prices of some petroleum products seemed unavoidable in order to meet the oil companies deficit."
And PTI reported that the spokesman said Gujral "conveyed that the question to be addressed now is which section of consumers need to be subsidised.
Gujral, in an interview with state-run Doordarshan television late on Thursday, said subsidies on LPG and diesel would be slashed.

He also said the government was willing to transfer the outstanding bill to oil companies --which was put at 190 billion rupees ($5.3 billion) in the interview-- for sales of petroleum products onto its own account.
The spokesman also said the Prime Minister had conveyed that several alternatives to bridge the gap were under study.
"The issue regarding the large deficit of nearly 190 billion rupees that keeps increasing, needs attention."
The United Front steering committee's meeting has been deferred three times so far, after two inconclusive earlier meetings.
There is no confirmation of a new date, but official sources said a core meeting of key decision makers is expected to held on July 17, and a steering committee would be held thereafter.
Indian oil companies are owed around 190 billion rupees ($5.32 billion) by the government for selling below market prices to support the country's subsidy regime.

The oil pool deficit ballooned after a surge in world prices last year, as home prices were left unchanged. At the end of 1996/97 (April-March), the deficit stood at 155 billion rupees. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
